tip: Month names and proper nouns take an apostrophe before a suffix: Haziran'da (Haziran + da = in June).
For half past, say the hour then buçuk: iki buçukta = at two and a half, meaning half past two.
The verb alışmak takes the dative: havaya alıştı = got used to the weather, hava plus ya.
Meğer flags a fact you just realized and pairs with the -miş past: gitmişiz = turns out we went.
The ending -la/-le means with: arkadaşımla = with my colleague, from arkadaşım plus la.
-abil- adds can, and as a question it becomes a polite request: açabilir misiniz = could you open.
-dığında means when something happens, attached to the verb: yapıldığında = when it is made.
The -erdi/-ardı ending is the habitual past, used to do: çizerdi = used to draw regularly.
Unreal wish: -sa on the condition, -irdim on the result. olsa ... alırdım = if I had ... I would buy.
-maktadır is a formal written present continuous, common in news: yapmaktadır = is making.
Comparisons use ablative -den plus daha: kardeşinden daha uzun = taller than the brother.
-dığım builds a relative clause, the thing that I did: gördüğüm manzara = the view that I saw.
Locative -da can mean per for frequency: haftada üç kez = three times a week.
Add -dır to a time span to mean for that long: yüzyıllardır = for centuries and still going.
-ip chains two verbs with one subject, and only the last carries tense: bulup getirdi = found and brought.
-an turns a verb into the one who does it, before a noun: spor yapan insan = people who exercise.
Past what-if: -seydi on the condition, -mazdı result. erimeseydi ... daralmazdı = if it hadn't melted, wouldn't have shrunk.
